page: Amazon Web Services i8g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARM64 processor. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaches 154.96 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 83.0 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is strong, placing in the top 25% at 14.14 GB/sec. However, cryptographic capabilities represent a performance tradeoff, as the PassMark CPU encryption test registers in the bottom 25% at 1507.35. For LLM workloads, prompt processing with a medium 7B model is poor, scoring in the bottom 10% at 15.47 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 11.0 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i8g.2xlarge offers high resource density by combining dedicated ARM64 cores with a substantial 1875 GB local NVMe SSD storage allocation and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This profile makes it suitable for storage-intensive and database workloads, such as Redis deployments, which benchmarked at 17.53 million SET operations per second, as well as static web serving and general database operations.
